title: A misdeclared returns_response retries forever at DEBUG and never sticky-disables
impact: ServiceValidationError subclasses HomeAssistantError, so a wrong `returns_response` flag lands in the handler documented as TRANSIENT-do-not-disable. It logs at DEBUG and returns; the next tick repeats. A one-word adapter config mistake becomes a permanent ~15s retry loop that never surfaces above debug. The ServiceNotFound/ServiceNotSupported branch exists precisely for 'this will never work' -- a misdeclared response contract belongs there.

title: get_map_bucket returns a DETACHED dict on a miss and live storage on a hit
impact: Mutation through the getter persists or silently vanishes depending on whether the map already exists -- the shape audit #1 found (a claim written to a copy). Sibling ensure_map_bucket uses setdefault and always returns storage. LATENT: 3 of 12 callers checked, all reads.

title: get_vacuum_maps_summary mixes a live room_count with CACHED enabled/disabled counts
impact: room_count is live len(rooms); enabled_room_count/disabled_room_count come from the stored summary block. Anything writing rooms without recomputing summary makes them disagree in one payload.

title: The dock-event timestamp is written BEFORE the debounce, so a debounced event still corrupts last_*
impact: CONFIRMS audit #12's A1-REG-1 from the receiving side. vacuum_events[event_type] = now runs unconditionally at :383; the debounce block at :388-424 gates only the COUNTER. So even where debounce is configured (Eufy declares it for last_mop_wash only), a restart or availability blip mid-cycle resets the 'last washed / last dried' timestamp shown on the Base Station tab.

title: record_dock_event validates nothing; its sibling set_dock_event_count validates the same vocabulary
impact: set_dock_event_count checks event_type against counter_map and returns {'updated': False, 'error': ...} for anything unknown. record_dock_event writes vacuum_events[event_type] = now for ANY string. Since event_type comes from adapter-declared triggers, a mis-declared trigger writes junk keys into durable storage permanently, unnoticed. Sibling divergence on one class.

title: A manual counter reset leaves the debounce marker, suppressing the next genuine event
impact: set_dock_event_count zeroes the counter but never clears {event_type}_last_counted_at. Reset inside the debounce window and the next real wash is silently not counted -- reset and debounce state are not kept coherent.

title: source_available reports True for a MISSING usage_hours attribute, and reset_maintenance's invalid_usage_hours is unreachable for it
impact: DOC-CHECKED against doc 13 §5.2: the `0.0 if unavailable` default is documented INTENT, so that half is not a defect. What remains: `.get('usage_hours', 0)` means a missing attribute never raises, so source_available is set True on a value that came from nowhere and the component reads as freshly serviced permanently (remaining = full interval). Same default makes reset_maintenance's documented 'invalid_usage_hours' failure reason unreachable for the missing case, so it returns reset:True -- and the service layer saves ONLY when reset is True, so the bogus baseline is what gets persisted. Line 369 in the same file handles absence correctly (-> None -> 'unknown').

title: exc_info tracebacks are stored UNREDACTED and UNTRUNCATED — both published claims hold only for the message field
impact: PROVEN by execution, not read. The forum post states 'Secrets (token/password/api_key/bearer) are masked before a record is stored' and 'Capping each message (I use ~2 kB, eliding the rest) is what actually killed the multi-MB dumps'. Line 163 redacts and truncates record.getMessage(); line 173-174 stores format_exception() with neither, and render_text writes it verbatim. Reproducer: one log.debug(..., exc_info=True) whose exception carries token=SUPERSECRET123 -> masked in the message, present TWICE in the dump file (the raise source line and the exception repr). A RuntimeError carrying 50 kB produced a 50,022-char line with no elision marker. The dump exists to be handed to a maintainer, and the module ships as a public MIT gist others are invited to copy, so both a leaked credential and the multi-MB regression propagate. Untested: test_redaction_masks_secrets covers only the message path, and the single test touching 'exc' hand-builds the dict instead of producing it through emit().

title: The switch bypasses the auto-stop bookkeeping the services maintain — forgotten override sibling at the entry-point layer
impact: max_minutes lives in an `autostop` dict closed over inside register_debug_services; only the start/stop SERVICES cancel it. DebugCaptureSwitch.async_turn_on/off call capture.start()/stop() directly and lexically cannot reach that closure. So a timer armed by the service silently stops a capture the user later started with the switch, and the switch can neither arm nor cancel one. The post advertises the two as interchangeable ('A toggle + dropdown instead of Dev Tools calls'), which is exactly the claim that fails.

title: Reload orphans a pending auto-stop timer
impact: `autostop` is re-created per register_debug_services call, so reloading the integration while a max_minutes timer is armed leaves the old async_call_later uncancellable. It fires later and stops an unrelated capture. Same seam as DR-DBG-2.

title: An unrecognised `areas` value silently produces a capture that records nothing
impact: _resolve_areas falls back to the substring f'.{a}' for any name not in the configured map. Via the UI the options are generated so they are always valid, but the debug_capture_start SERVICE takes free-form strings: `areas: ['maps']` (the real key is 'map') yields a filter matching no logger. Capture reports active, seen stays 0, the dump is empty, and nothing warns. Silent wrong answer on the diagnostic tool itself.

title: The restore guard cannot distinguish its own DEBUG from a user's mid-capture `logger:` DEBUG
impact: The post claims stop 'restores the prior level + propagate — but only if they're still the values it installed, so it won't clobber a logger: change you made mid-capture.' True for any level EXCEPT debug: the guard is `logger.level == logging.DEBUG`, so a user who sets the integration to debug during a capture has it silently reverted on stop. The one level a debugging user is most likely to pick.
wontfix: Reaching it requires starting the flight recorder — a tool whose entire purpose is to avoid enabling `logger:` debug — and then enabling `logger:` debug anyway, mid-capture. That is a user footgun, not a defect: the two actions contradict each other. Documented in the module and in the post rather than guarded against.

title: status() reports stale started_at / services / areas after a stop
impact: stop() clears _ring, _logger_name and the prior-state fields but leaves _areas, _targets and _started_at. debug_capture_status then returns active: False beside a populated services list and a started_at from the finished run, reading as a live capture on the tool's own diagnostic surface.

title: Two dumps in the same second overwrite each other
impact: The dump filename is second-resolution (debug-%Y%m%d-%H%M%S.log) and so is the .tmp path. Two dumps inside one second silently collide -- plausible when the switch auto-dumps on off and the user also calls debug_capture_dump.

title: "Everything in _vacuum_diagnostics is read-only" is false — refresh=False does not make the capability call inert
impact: The module docstring EXCLUDES the dashboard snapshot on read-only grounds ('computing it can advance room timing and fire room-transition events during a live clean, and a diagnostics download must stay read-only'), and line 570 asserts the rest is read-only. get_vacuum_capabilities(refresh=False) is not: ensure_vacuum_record() setdefaults into self.data['vacuums'], line 1183 setdefaults self.data['capabilities'], and THREE paths call refresh_vacuum_capabilities despite refresh=False -- no stored snapshot, stored lacking detected_model, and the model_family self-heal mismatch -- each assigning self.data['capabilities'][vacuum_entity_id] = payload after running full model detection. That method's own docstring says so out loud: 'detection runs even if refresh=False'. The author passed the flag believing it bought read-only; it does not. Campaign signature shape -- a comment asserting a guard, where the guard does not hold, and here a deliberate exclusion elsewhere in the same docstring rests on it. Bites hardest in the scenario support actually asks for: download diagnostics WHILE the problem is happening. PRECISION: in steady state this IS effectively read-only -- ensure_vacuum_record's setdefault is a no-op on an existing record, and the self-heal comment is right that a matching family never re-detects. The writes are certain on a fresh or storage-reset install (stored is None) and on a post-update family mismatch. So the defect is the CLAIM, which a future collector will be added against, more than today's behaviour.

title: Nine repr(err) sinks bypass the key-based redaction the docstring promises unconditionally
impact: async_redact_data matches KEYS. capabilities_error, maps_error, upkeep_snapshot_error, roborock_geometry_drift_error, vacuums_error, integration_version_error, completion_health.error, area_units.error and managed_rooms_by_map[<id>].error each hold a free-text repr(err) under a key not in TO_REDACT, so anything inside an exception message reaches the downloaded file verbatim. The docstring states 'Credentials are redacted' with no qualifier. Same class as DR-DBG-1, which was PROVEN in the sibling module; here the structural gap is certain but no credential-carrying exception was demonstrated reaching one of these sinks, so it is reported as a gap, not a leak.

title: A failed health probe is silently absent from the warnings block designed to be read first
impact: _self_check appends completion_health['warning'] and area_units['warning'] into `warnings` -- described as 'loud, actionable warnings that belong at the top of a support read'. Both collectors instead produce {'error': repr(err)} when they throw, and an error key is never surfaced. So when the probe that detects 'EVERY run will strand' fails to run at all, the block a support helper reads first is silently clean. The raw dict survives further down, but the signal is exactly what self_check exists to raise.

title: entry.title is dumped unredacted while entry.data and entry.options are redacted
impact: Only data and options pass through async_redact_data. The title is user-settable free text on the config entry, dumped verbatim. Low, but it is the same field class as `notes`, which TO_REDACT covers precisely because it is 'a classic place users paste account passwords'.

title: Dead `_SENTINELS` alias sits in the one file whose header explains why that set must not fork
impact: _SENTINELS = BLANK_STATE_VALUES is assigned and never read; the live use is _ACTIVE_MAP_SENTINELS, which IS BLANK_STATE_VALUES (same object, correctly centralized). So the file carries a second, unused name for the same set directly beneath a comment explaining that this set must match the importer's or the self-check reports 'everything works' for a device the importer refuses. Harmless today; it is an invitation to create exactly the divergence the comment guards against.

title: remap_confirmed_floor_types mutates in place while iterating, losing confirmations whenever old and new id sets overlap
impact: PROVEN by execution. The loop pops str(old_id) and writes str(new_id) into the SAME dict it is iterating over, so a new_id that is also a later old_id consumes the entry just written. Measured: id_remap={1:2, 2:3, 3:4} with rooms 1,2,3 confirmed yields {'4': True} -- 2 of 3 confirmations destroyed. A swap {1:2, 2:1} moves the confirmation onto the WRONG room. Disjoint remaps ({16:27}) are correct, which is why it looks fine: EVERY existing test uses a disjoint remap, so the defect is invisible to the suite by construction. Overlap is not exotic -- it is what happens whenever a device re-segments and reissues ids from the same range, while the disjoint case needs it to jump to a fresh block. The consequence is precisely what this function's own docstring says it exists to prevent: renumbered-but-confirmed rooms read as unconfirmed and the start gate blocks cleaning with onboarding_required. Fix is a new dict rather than in-place mutation.

title: check_for_new_rooms compares a PER-MAP stored count against a source with no map scoping
impact: The stored side, room_count_at_last_check, is stamped by mark_rooms_discovered from data['maps'][vacuum][map_id]['rooms'] -- per map. The live side reads the vacuum entity's `segments` attribute, which carries only the ACTIVE map's rooms and has no map_id in it at all. So the function is parameterized by map_id but only half its comparison honours it: on a multi-map vacuum, asking about any non-active map compares two different maps' room counts and returns an arbitrary answer. Latent today (doc code-flag CS-2 records no live caller) but the doc explicitly invites wiring it -- 'A caller would decide whether to show a notification' -- and the signature advertises a scoping the body does not have. A trap laid for the next person.

title: The 'empty means complete' guard exists in setup/status.py and was never mirrored onto the onboarding summary — forgotten override sibling
impact: UPGRADED from LOW after finding the sibling that HAS the guard. Both sites answer the same question with the same optimistic-accumulator shape: setup/status.py initialises all_steps_complete=True and all_in_sync=True and only sets them False INSIDE `for vac in managed:`, so an empty managed set leaves both True -- and line 218 defends exactly that with `setup_complete = bool(managed) and all_steps_complete and all_in_sync`. onboarding/manager.py:239 has the identical shape (any_incomplete=False, set True only inside `for map_id in maps.keys():`) and NO equivalent term, so all_complete is vacuously True for a vacuum with zero maps; sensor/onboarding.py:62 then falls through both scan loops and reports 'complete'. So the fix was made once, on the surface the card reads, and never carried to the diagnostic sensor. Doc 18 §4.5 records the behaviour as 'vacuous truth' without recognising a sibling had already rejected it. User-visible: the ONBOARDING sensor asserts setup is finished at the one moment it is most consulted -- fresh install, nothing imported, 'why can't I schedule a job?'. Fix mirrors line 218: require a non-empty maps collection, or add a distinct not_started state.

title: The five-key default record is hand-duplicated between _get_map_onboarding and reset_onboarding
impact: Lines 66-72 and 252-258 are two hand-maintained copies of one vocabulary -- the campaign's structural root cause, in a 263-line module. A sixth flag added to the lazy-create path silently produces reset records missing it, and vice versa; nothing derives one from the other. Compounding it, two of the five keys (discovery_notified, rebuild_notified) are already dead (doc code-flag CS-1: never read, never set True), so the duplication is maintaining fields nobody consumes. One shared default constant or builder closes it.

title: The sensor recomputes the entire onboarding summary twice per update
impact: native_value and extra_state_attributes each call _get_summary() independently, and each call iterates every map building a full get_onboarding_state dict. A polling diagnostic entity does the whole aggregation twice per write for one state update.

title: Doc cites the start gate at core/manager.py:2776; it is at 2805
impact: The CLAIM is correct -- the gate really does block on floor_types_complete alone and never consults rooms_discovered. Only the line reference drifted. Recorded because this doc's stated scope is that 'a developer should be able to re-implement the onboarding manager from this document alone', which makes its source references part of the contract.

title: Doc §3 states the MAX_DELTA_PCT boundary one step off from the code and from its own §5.2
impact: The tunable-constants table says 'Reject single-sample deltas this large OR LARGER' (>= 3.0). manager.py:524 is `if abs(raw_delta) <= MAX_DELTA_PCT`, so exactly 3.0 is ACCEPTED and only >3.0 is rejected -- which is what doc §5.2's own snippet shows. The table is the half a tuner reads before changing the value, and it is the half that is wrong.

title: An out-of-order sample is correctly skipped but still rewinds the last-sample anchor
impact: Line 522 guards the delta block with `if elapsed_sec > 0`, so a sample whose timestamp is not newer contributes no drain/rate -- correct. But lines 601-603 then commit last_battery_level / last_sample_ts unconditionally, including the older values. The NEXT sample computes its delta against the rewound anchor, so one stale observation can inflate or suppress the following drain or rate. Narrow: needs an out-of-order state event, plausible mainly at startup where _sample_now(now) can race a queued event with an earlier time_fired. The guard is right; the commit is simply not gated by it.

title: After a stale-session discard, charging stays untracked until the next charge cycle
impact: _update_session discards a session older than SESSION_MAX_HOURS and sets session=None. Control then reaches `if session is None: return` (line 680) on every later sample, because prev_charging is already True so the open branch never fires. No replacement session opens while the vacuum keeps charging; tracking resumes only after charging flips false and true again. Doc §6.5 documents the discard and its purpose but not this consequence.

title: Doc omits two live conditions present in the code
impact: §6.4/§8 give the mid-job rate-stat gate as `kind == 'mid_job' and avg > 0`; manager.py:771 also requires `delta_pct > 0`. §5.2's _process_sample snippet omits the `elapsed_sec > 0` guard at line 522 entirely. Both are correct code and sensible guards -- the doc is what is incomplete, and its stated scope is re-implementation from the document alone.

title: The active_job sensor reports 'none' during an app-started run the system itself considers in flight
impact: native_value hand-enumerates started / paused / completed and defaults everything else to 'none'. But `external` is a first-class status in this codebase: jobs/active_job.py:136 puts it in _RUN_IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES so run_is_in_flight() returns True for it, :1856 seeds a slot with status='external' for app-started runs, and learning/external_run.py:93 branches on it. So while the vacuum is actively cleaning on an app-started run -- with an in-flight record and learning capturing it -- this sensor reads 'none'. Compounded by sensor/error.py:89-92, whose docstring tells consumers to 'Use sensor.<obj>_active_job to tell which sub-case applies' when disambiguating 'no active run' from 'active run with no errors yet'; that instruction returns the wrong answer for exactly the run type audit #3 was about. The class docstring calls it a 'five-value enum', so the omission is baked into the stated contract. Textbook centralize-the-question: the shared vocabulary exists one module away and this consumer hand-copied a subset with a permissive default.

title: Two ~40-line dynamic-entity reconciliation blocks are hand-duplicated and must be edited in lockstep
impact: _sync_room_history_entities and _sync_room_rule_status_entities are byte-identical apart from the entity-dict name -- same prefix derivation, same stale-id scan, same registry removal, same add path, same refresh helper. Verified in sync TODAY, so this is a maintenance hazard rather than a defect: any fix to the reconciliation (a prefix collision, a registry-removal edge, an unremoved entity) lands in one copy unless someone remembers the other. This is the structural root cause the campaign keeps finding, sitting in the platform that creates entities dynamically as rooms change.

title: Deleting map N from vacuum.X sweeps every entity of vacuum.X_N from the registry
impact: PROVEN. Room entity ids are make_room_unique_id -> {vac_key}_{map_id}_{room_id}_{suffix}. The post-delete registry sweep matches on {vac_key}_{map_id}_, so deleting map 2 from vacuum.alfred builds prefix vacuum_alfred_2_ -- which every entity of the SEPARATE vacuum vacuum.alfred_2 starts with, on EVERY map. Measured: all 8 of the sibling entities across two maps matched, and registry.async_remove deletes them. That loses name/area/icon/hidden customisations and releases the entity_id reservations, so entities can return under different ids and silently break automations and dashboards. The result reports entities_removed: N without saying whose. HA auto-suffixes a duplicate entity_id with _2, so vacuum.alfred plus vacuum.alfred_2 is an ordinary two-vacuum install and Eufy map ids are small integers -- uncommon, not exotic. Sharp detail: the trailing underscore DOES correctly prevent the map_id 2-vs-20 collision (verified as a control), so the prefix was designed against one ambiguity axis and misses the other. Seven sites hand-copy the pattern (sensor/__init__.py x4, number.py:101, switch.py:71, delete.py:136); only delete.py removes, but the others mark entities stale on the same match. ESCALATION (agent-found, verified at source): not limited to the two-vacuum case. adapters/roborock/adapter.py:190 documents its active-map entity select.{id}_selected_map as reporting the map NAME ('Main floor'), and get_active_map_id returns str(state.state) verbatim, so on Roborock a map_id is a human string that can contain underscores. Maps named 'Main' and 'Main_floor' collide WITHIN one vacuum. That removes the 'needs two similarly-named vacuums' precondition entirely for Roborock users. A second agent independently confirmed the {map}_{room} boundary is NOT ambiguous (room_id is int-coerced), so the ambiguity is confined to the vacuum_key<->map_id boundary -- i.e. exactly this finding, and nowhere else.

title: auto_refresh_on still uses the bare or-coercion that code-flag CS-2 fixed for its three siblings
impact: get_discovery_cadence reads list(disc.get(auto_refresh_on) or _DEFAULT_AUTO_REFRESH_TRIGGERS). The other three keys in the same dict literal were converted to an is-not-None guard precisely because or silently reverts a configured falsy value to the default -- doc 15 section 4.5 records that as CS-2, fixed and regression-tested as DR-15. An empty list is the meaningful wire-no-auto-discovery-triggers setting, and it is exactly what or eats: an adapter declaring auto_refresh_on: [] silently gets vacuum_docked + active_map_changed + config_entry_reload. Confirmed meaningful at the consumer, listeners/discovery.py:73, whose own trailing or-empty-list is dead code since the cadence can never return empty -- evidence its author expected [] to be reachable. The doc table records the or form accurately and does not notice it is the bug it flags two rows down.

title: Two unguarded int(key) coercions on drift-history keys, in a module that guards every other one
impact: The stale-entry prune and the history-only new-room branch both coerce a storage key with no try/except, while _room_lookup and _list_configured_room_ids in the same file wrap identical coercions in except (TypeError, ValueError): continue. Keys are written as str(rid) so they should always parse; a hand-edited or migrated record with a non-numeric key raises ValueError out of update_drift_history and compute_room_drift, taking the whole setup-status response with it.

title: Protection evaluation calls .get() on map buckets and room records without isinstance guards
impact: The imported-map comprehension and the has_rules / has_access_graph scans assume dicts, where drift.py consistently checks isinstance(bucket, dict) first. A malformed record raises AttributeError out of evaluate_map_protection, which both the delete gate and the per-map summaries in get_setup_status call -- so one bad room record takes out the whole Setup tab. Fails closed on the destructive path, hence LOW, but it is the inconsistent half of a defensive convention the sibling module keeps.

title: A managed vacuum with no imported map gets ZERO per-vacuum sensors, and importing a map never creates them
impact: VERIFIED AT SOURCE. The per-vacuum loop is `maps = manager.data.get('maps', {}); for vacuum_entity_id in maps.keys()`, and EVERY per-vacuum sensor is built inside it: onboarding, theme, dock events, profiles, map overlays, both error sensors, all maintenance and all battery sensors. data['maps'][vac] is created ONLY by the import path (maps/map_manager.py:17-19, confirmed the only writers); ensure_vacuum_record and async_initialize seed vacuums/capabilities/room_history but never maps. There is also no add-path -- all four registered manager callbacks are room-scoped. setup_add_vacuum DOES reload the entry, but at reload time the map does not exist yet, and setup_import_active_map creates the map and does NOT reload. Net: a vacuum finishes onboarding with per-room sensors (built by the room callbacks) and none of its per-vacuum sensors, until an unrelated restart. Sibling contrast that names the bug: button.py:32 iterates data['vacuums'], so maintenance RESET BUTTONS exist for a vacuum whose maintenance SENSORS do not. Also makes doc 18 §4.5's documented zero-map behaviour unreachable -- the sensor is not absent-and-lying, it is simply absent.

title: The maintenance sensor's documented availability guard never fires; it publishes a fabricated full-life value
impact: CONSUMER SIDE OF DR-MNT-1 -- same root cause at maintenance/manager.py:713. CLUSTER THESE. The class docstring claims 'Returns available = False (and native_value = None) when the source entity is unavailable so stale hours are never silently reported' -- a claim, not evidence. source_available is set True whenever hass.states.get(source) is not None, which holds for an UNAVAILABLE entity; it returns None only when the entity does not exist. HA drops extra_state_attributes while unavailable, so usage_hours is absent, the `, 0` default wins, and current_usage becomes 0.0 with source_available True. Repro (numbers corrected by Stage B execution -- my original prose transposed them): a healthy source at 108h against a 66h baseline reads native_value 108.0 / used_since_reset 42.0; the upstream integration reloads; the next poll reports 150.0h remaining, used_since_reset 0.0, source_available true, and the warning transition never fires. state_class measurement means the recorder ingests the fabricated value into long-term statistics. Sibling proof in the same module: maintenance/manager.py:369 uses .get('usage_hours') with NO default, so a missing attribute raises and yields an honest None.

title: Two of the four sensor prefix sites are destructive - a room sync on one vacuum deletes a sibling's registry entries
impact: Per-site verdict extending DR-SETUP-1. :255 (_sync_room_history_entities) and :312 (_sync_room_rule_status_entities) compute stale_ids by prefix and then call _registry.async_remove() -- DESTRUCTIVE. :285 and :341 only push a state write -- benign, since each entity re-reads its own storage slot. Repro: vacuum.alfred (maps 1,2) and vacuum.alfred_2 (maps 1,3) both managed; deleting map 2 from vacuum.alfred leaves rooms={} so desired_entities={}, prefix 'vacuum_alfred_2_', and stale_ids captures vacuum.alfred_2's LIVE room sensors on maps that were never touched. Registry removal discards the user's entity_id override, custom name, icon, area and hidden/disabled flags. setup/delete.py:136 then runs its own sweep with the same prefix and NO dict-membership constraint, additionally matching the sibling's theme, dock, overlays, active_job, maintenance and battery entities -- so the blast radius of one map deletion is every eufy_vacuum entity of the sibling vacuum. Agent flags a needs-runtime-check tail: registry removal is synchronous but entity async_remove is an un-awaited task, so a re-add racing it can be rejected for a duplicate unique_id and left permanently missing with hass=None while the tracking dict insists it exists.

title: Renaming a room never reaches the entity's friendly name - the rebuilt entity carrying the new name is discarded
impact: VERIFIED: async_update_entity has ZERO occurrences anywhere in the integration. Both sync blocks construct a fresh entity per desired room and then discard it when the unique_id is already known, pushing only a state write. EufyVacuumRoomEntity captures the room name once into _attr_translation_placeholders, which HA resolves at add-time. So after a rename via setup_save_rooms, extra_state_attributes['room_name'] updates correctly and the card shows the new name, while the entity's friendly name keeps the old one in the entity list, dashboards and voice exposure until a restart. Half-updated state that presents as a card bug.

title: The overlays sensor serves a cache entry without checking its map_id or its stale flag
impact: _result() reads cache[vac]['result'] and ignores cache[vac]['map_id'] -- a key the producer maintains precisely so consumers cannot mix maps: map_source_coordinator.py:117 guards the hold path with cached.get('map_id') == str(map_id) and comments 'never serve another map's geometry.' That guard is wired into the writer and not the reader: forgotten-override-sibling shape. Repro: at restart the initial warm runs while active_map is still blank, so the fallback takes the first stored map by insertion order; a vacuum actually on map 2 gets map 1's geometry and room list published as current_room for up to 60s -- and the sensor's stated purpose is recorder history. Separately the reader exposes none of the producer's stale / stale_since / stale_reason keys, so it reports present:true with frozen geometry for up to a 6-hour TTL with no signal. NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED by the orchestrator.

title: Setting the GLOBAL default theme returns without notifying, so the theme sensor is stale indefinitely
impact: VERIFIED AT SOURCE. set_active_theme's `if vacuum_entity_id is None:` branch writes theme['default_theme_id'] and returns immediately; the per-vacuum branch two lines below ends with self._notify_updated(...). Every other mutation in the file notifies. The sensor is _attr_should_poll = False, doc 02 §4 says it updates exclusively via the theme callback, and frontend/theme-system.md:366 states 'After EVERY mutation the manager calls _notify_updated()'. So calling set_active_theme with vacuum_entity_id omitted -- explicitly permitted by the service schema -- updates storage while the sensor's default_theme_id attribute keeps the old value until some unrelated theme mutation happens to fire. Forgotten override sibling inside one function, two branches apart.

title: The stated thread-safety invariant is internally inconsistent, and copies 3 and 4 have already dropped it
impact: Extends DR-SENS-2. _request_entity_state_write asserts manager callbacks may fire from worker threads so all refreshes must funnel through it. If that premise holds, then hass.async_create_task, er.async_get + async_remove, and async_add_entities in the SAME callbacks are all loop-affine and unprotected -- the funnel guards the least dangerous of the four. If it does not hold, the funnel is unnecessary. Both cannot be true. The agent traced every producer and found them loop-only today, so it is latent. The load-bearing half: switch.py:88 and number.py:118 call existing.async_write_ha_state() DIRECTLY, having copied every other line of the same stale/add/remove logic -- the block now exists in four copies plus a fifth variant in setup/delete.py, and has already diverged on exactly the point its own docstring calls mandatory. This is the argument for one shared sync_room_entities helper rather than four patches.

title: active_job_entities and its explanatory comment are dead
impact: The dict is documented as keyed by (vacuum, map) 'so the job-finished handler can refresh the right sensor directly', and is populated, but never read; _handle_job_finished refreshes only room-history sensors. Behaviour is not lost -- EufyVacuumActiveJobSensor subscribes to EVENT_JOB_FINISHED itself plus a tracker listener, EVENT_ROOM_STARTED and a 5-minute safety net. So this is dead state plus a comment describing behaviour that does not exist: the campaign's own top rule pointed at itself.

title: native_value returns the literal string 'unavailable', colliding with HA's reserved state
impact: VERIFIED AT SOURCE: `if not res.get('present'): return 'unavailable'`. That is indistinguishable in hass.states, templates, is_state() and the frontend from an entity that is genuinely unavailable, while the real diagnostic sits in attrs['reason']. A sentinel is the right idea; this specific sentinel aliases a reserved value. 'no_map' -- or available=False with native_value None -- carries the same information without the collision.

title: panels.py claims to be the single registration seam; a fourth site hand-copies all three of its constants
impact: VERIFIED AT SOURCE. The module docstring asserts it is 'the single source of truth for that registration so the three call sites all compute the title and register the panel identically'. There are FOUR sites, and the fourth is in __init__.py:428-441 -- the same file that imports async_register_vacuum_panel -- re-typing webcomponent_name='eufy-vacuum-command-center', sidebar_title='Vacuum Agent' and sidebar_icon='mdi:robot-vacuum' as literals. Confirmed those are exactly panels.WEBCOMPONENT_NAME, DEFAULT_PANEL_TITLE and PANEL_ICON (panels.py:29-31), and that the three constants have no readers outside panels.py. The fourth site is the FALLBACK panel, which a fresh install with no vacuum yet hits exclusively. So renaming the frontend custom element updates panels.py, keeps every existing user working, and gives new users a blank sidebar panel with no error and no other way to add a vacuum -- onboarding dead on arrival for the population least able to diagnose it. doc 02 §11 repeats the 'three call sites' claim verbatim, so the doc is wrong in the same way and never mentions the fallback panel.

title: _LOCAL_TZ is a FIXED offset captured at import, so naive legacy timestamps get the wrong offset half the year
impact: VERIFIED BY EXECUTION. `_LOCAL_TZ = datetime.now().astimezone().tzinfo` does not return a DST-aware zone -- it returns a datetime.timezone with a frozen offset. Ran it: repr is datetime.timezone(timedelta(-1, 61200), 'Pacific Daylight Time') and utcoffset() is -7:00 for BOTH 2026-01-15 and 2026-07-15, despite the label. parse_timestamp's default path (assume_local_naive=True) therefore stamps every naive value with the import-time offset rather than the one in force on the timestamp's own date. Repro: HA restarts 2026-01-10 in America/New_York so _LOCAL_TZ is fixed -05:00; a legacy naive value '2026-07-15 14:00:00' (written during EDT, true instant 18:00Z) parses to 19:00Z -- one hour late. The error does NOT cancel when one endpoint is legacy-naive and the other is a modern Z value, which is the mixed-vintage case in room_history. Consumers are the duration/staleness readers in learning/ and core/manager.py's _hours_since. HONEST BOUND: +/-1 hour, and only for records still in the pre-migration naive form -- every current writer emits Z. Notably no test exercises the default assume_local_naive=True path at all, so _LOCAL_TZ is never evaluated under test despite the 98% coverage figure for the module.

title: VacuumCapabilities is a never-constructed dataclass whose field names do not exist in the real capability payload
impact: The live capability map is built by core/capabilities.py:353-400. Five of VacuumCapabilities' fields do not exist in it: supports_map_selection (real key supports_active_map), supports_dock_empty (real key supports_empty_dust), supports_live_map and supports_maintenance_entities (no equivalent), and tested_profile (real key model_family). A grep for those five names returns only their declarations. Nothing constructs the dataclass or calls as_dict(). The hazard is that a dataclass with an as_dict() in the package the architecture doc calls the canonical model layer INVITES exactly that wiring, and doing so produces a bucket whose five renamed keys silently read False at every consumer -- dock-empty, map-switching and maintenance controls vanish from the card with no error. tests/unit/test_models.py MOD-3 round-trips the dataclass against its own fields, so it green-lights the stale names. doc 03 documents the real shape and never mentions this dataclass.

title: The BLANK_STATE_VALUES docstring asserts a consolidation that is roughly 20% applied
impact: The comment states the hand-copied variants 'existed at six sites and had drifted into three shapes', in the past tense as resolved. Three modules import the shared name (diagnostics.py, mapping/tracker.py, rooms/room_discovery.py) while four still hand-copy the byte-identical set: listeners/lifecycle.py:57, adapters/eufy/lifecycle.py:67, jobs/active_job.py:2373 (inline frozenset fallback) and adapters/eufy/adapter.py:436 -- plus one already-DIVERGENT copy at adapters/eufy/discovery.py:56, which carries capital-None and lacks 'null'. Impact today is nil since membership matches, but the module's stated purpose ('so a caller cannot drift by re-listing members') is unachieved for the majority of callers, so the next member added reaches 3 of 8 sites. Same shape as the ~80%-applied adapter seam, inverted.

title: The unique-id scheme is a non-injective flat join with no parser, and its vacuum-key half is open-coded at four sites
impact: Extends DR-SETUP-1 on the CONSTRUCTION side. The join f'{vacuum_key}_{map_id}_{room_id}_{suffix}' uses '_' as separator while three of the four fields may contain '_', and there is NO companion parse function anywhere -- which is why every consumer resorts to prefix matching. Useful negative result: the agent could not construct a within-one-vacuum collision at the {map}_{room} boundary, because room_id is int-coerced at room_entities.py:37, so 'Floor'+12 -> Floor_12 stays decidable against 'Floor_1'+2 -> Floor_1_2. The ambiguity is confined to the vacuum_key<->map_id boundary. The fix-surface problem: the vacuum_entity_id.replace('.','_') sanitisation whose ambiguity IS the known HIGH is open-coded at battery/sensors.py:131, sensor/error.py:46, button.py:168 and __init__.py:699, with no make_vacuum_unique_id helper -- so fixing make_room_unique_id alone leaves vacuum.alfred and vacuum.alfred_2 still colliding in build_vacuum_device_info's DEVICE identifier and in those four builders. __init__.py:697-705 already documents that it cannot reverse '_'->'.' and carries a sanitisation-collision branch: the code knows the join is lossy and works around it per-site.

title: The repair flow is unreachable - nothing ever raises an issue - and the doc asserts the opposite
impact: VERIFIED: a repo-wide grep for async_create_issue / ir.create_issue across custom_components returns ZERO hits, so async_create_fix_flow is never invoked. doc 02 §10 states 'Currently raised by the setup workflow when state is inconsistent (vacuum not found, map not imported)' -- neither setup/workflow.py nor services/setup.py imports issue_registry. Three latent consequences: strings.json declares issues.onboarding_required in all 18 language packs for an issue that is never created; that block has no fix_flow section, so a raised issue would render a form with no title or body; and ConfirmRepairFlow is imported and never used while EufyVacuumSetupRedirectFlow hand-reimplements it (without the data_schema HA's version passes). No raised-but-never-cleared bug exists -- the dismissal path is the correct idiom. The defect is that the subsystem is wired to nothing while the doc says it is live.

title: Four constants are defined and never read - including three service names for services that do not exist
impact: Scripted check across every .py excluding const.py, cross-checked against services.yaml and the frontend bundle: SERVICE_REFRESH_BACKEND ('refresh_backend'), SERVICE_REBUILD_ACTIVE_MAP ('rebuild_active_map') and SERVICE_CLEAR_RUNTIME_STATE ('clear_runtime_state') have no async_register, no services.yaml entry and no occurrence in src/; DATA_SERVICES_REGISTERED has no reader. The other 137 names all have readers, and no const value is re-typed elsewhere except the panels trio (INF-1). Cosmetic -- but const.py is the file a brand port is told to consult, so three dead service names read as capability that does not exist.

title: The one call site step_types' docstring reasons about by name hand-copies the tuple instead of importing it
impact: step_types.py's docstring says 'The leading/trailing break-trim in planning.run_plan is deliberately the second set too' and closes with 'a caller that reaches for the set is one `and` clause away from re-creating the drift this module removes.' run_plan.py:883 then declares _BREAKS = ('charge_wait','wait') locally and uses it at four places; run_plan.py imports nothing from step_types. Membership is identical today, so impact is nil. The exposure: the module exists BECAUSE this vocabulary drifted twice in one day, its docstring names this exact site, and this is the one place still carrying a private copy -- so a fourth dock-polled phase type would update phase_runner, active_job and job_finalizer (all correct importers) and silently not the trim.

title: get_floor_type_label emits hardcoded English into an 18-language product
impact: Nine English literals plus an English-derived fallback (str(floor_type).replace('_',' ').title()), emitted as floor_type_label from three backend payloads (core/manager.py:280, planning/run_plan.py:174, profiles/manager.py:286). The card already has the correct implementation -- src/i18n/en.js:1341-1348 defines setup.floor_hardwood .. setup.floor_carpet_low_pile keyed by floor VALUE and rendered via t(). The backend field is read into src/state/rooms.js and passed through renderers but never rendered by any template, so it is dead payload today. The harm is a pre-built English string sitting in three service responses one t() call away from being displayed untranslated -- violating the no-string-without-i18n rule at the point of creation.

title: The maintenance reset button discards a documented failure result and reports success
impact: VERIFIED. async_press calls reset_maintenance(), throws the return value away, and unconditionally awaits async_save(). reset_maintenance is a result-returning API with three documented failure exits -- {'reset': False, 'reason': 'no_source_entity'|'source_unavailable'|'invalid_usage_hours'} -- and mutates nothing on any of them (doc 13 §5.4 states the contract verbatim). The sibling caller of the SAME method, the reset_maintenance service, does inspect payload['reset'] and raises ServiceValidationError. Reachable because _detect_maintenance_sources accepts a source that exists in the entity registry with NO state object, so the button is created for an upstream sensor that is not yet loaded / disabled / offline at start; pressing it returns source_unavailable, which is discarded. HA stamps a fresh press timestamp for every ButtonEntity press, so the UI shows success; there is no exception and no log line at any level, and the maintenance clock keeps running from the old baseline. Purest forgotten-override sibling, and it sits 80 lines above a class carrying a six-line comment about how a silently-swallowed call made a button 'do nothing'.

title: number.py's prefix sweep also destroys NON-room maintenance entities that its callback can never rebuild
impact: VERIFIED AT SOURCE, and this escalates DR-SETUP-1 on a second axis. number.py populates ONE entity_map with both the per-room order numbers AND the per-component maintenance-interval numbers ({vacuum_key}_{component}_maintenance_interval). The stale sweep matches anything in that map by prefix, but `desired` is rebuilt ONLY from _build_room_numbers. So a matched maintenance-interval number is popped, async_remove()'d and registry-removed -- and no code path in _on_rooms_updated ever reconstructs it. Room numbers come back on the next room update; the maintenance numbers return only on a full reload or restart. Two further escalations: (a) both destructive sites do a REGISTRY delete, permanently discarding the user's name/icon/area/category and enabled/hidden flags -- not a 'mark stale'; (b) the trigger is far wider than map deletion, since _on_rooms_updated runs on EVERY _notify_rooms_updated for that (vacuum, map) -- a routine room settings save, a drift pass, a queue-break edit. So with vacuum.alfred and vacuum.alfred_2 both configured, merely changing a room's fan speed on alfred map 2 deletes alfred_2's maintenance-interval controls. The guard EXISTS in both siblings and only number.py lacks it: button.py:166 appends a literal 'run_profile_' segment that makes its prefix collision-proof, and switch.py:48 deliberately keeps the integration-level debug switch out of entity_map entirely.

title: Interval bounds are framework constants, and the ceiling is BELOW a shipped component's declared max
impact: VERIFIED: MAINTENANCE_INTERVAL_MAX = 500.0 is applied to every component of every brand, while the adapter declares a per-component max_interval_hours that the schema marks REQUIRED -- and Eufy's `sensor` component declares 720. Doc 13 §6 already flags the over-permissive half as code-flag CS-3 (the adapter ceiling is not enforced at the write path); this is the UNDER-permissive half it does not record. The card renders min=1/max=720 from the adapter and the service schema has no max, so a user can store 720 -- after which the number entity reports native_value 720.0 against its own advertised native_max_value of 500.0, and any number.set_value of 720 raises ServiceValidationError from HA core. The user can read the value through the entity but can never restore it there. Symmetrically cleaning_tray declares 90 and the entity happily accepts 500. HONEST BOUND: every other shipped component on both brands is <= 450, so only Eufy `sensor` trips it, and only if the user raises the interval past 500.

title: Module comment asserts 'no polling'; the one class that polls is the one relying on it
impact: The comment `# All number entities write directly to manager storage; no polling.` sits above PARALLEL_UPDATES = 0. Verified as a claim: NumberEntity, unlike ButtonEntity, does NOT set _attr_should_poll = False, and EufyVacuumMaintenanceIntervalNumber never sets it -- so it is polled at the platform's 30s SCAN_INTERVAL. Every other class in the six files is genuinely poll-free. The two omissions cancel out, which is the interesting part: async_set_native_value mutates storage and saves but never calls async_write_ha_state(), and it is only non-stale because should_poll=True makes HA write the state after the service call. Adding _attr_should_poll = False to match the comment and the five siblings would FREEZE the entity. Observable defect today is milder: a 30s lag after a card-side interval save, plus unbounded PARALLEL_UPDATES on a platform documented as event-driven.

title: The saved-run-profile button name is hardcoded English, bypassing the translation mechanism
impact: Every other entity class in scope declares _attr_translation_key and lets HA resolve the name from strings.json. EufyVacuumSavedRunProfileButton sets _attr_has_entity_name = True, declares NO translation key, and overrides name with f'Run {profile_name}' plus a hardcoded 'Saved Run' fallback. strings.json and translations/en.json contain exactly one entity.button key (maintenance_reset), so there is nothing to translate against in any of the 18 shipped language packs. German HA with a profile named 'Kueche' renders 'Alfred Run Kueche' -- the verb stays English in every locale. Violates the no-string-without-i18n rule, and doc 02 §3 states the convention this class is the sole exception to without carving out an exception.

title: _attr_suggested_object_id is not a Home Assistant attribute - four sites rely on a dead assignment
impact: VERIFIED BY EXECUTION against the installed HA: Entity has NO _attr_suggested_object_id (hasattr False); suggested_object_id exists only as a READ-ONLY property derived from the entity's resolved name, and _async_derive_object_ids never consults an _attr_ backing field. The assignment sets an attribute nothing reads. ORCHESTRATOR ESCALATION: the agent found this in binary_sensor.py, but the pattern is at FOUR sites -- battery/sensors.py:139, binary_sensor.py:86, sensor/error.py:49 and sensor/lifecycle.py:70. No user-visible defect today: the entity IDs those four intend happen to be what HA derives anyway, because the translated name matches the suffix. The defect is that the guarantee is unenforced and believed -- the module docstrings and doc 02/doc 23 all assert the ID shape, so editing a name in strings.json silently changes four families of entity IDs while the dead lines and the docs keep asserting the old ones.

title: _async_update_room silently drops non-managed keys from a mixed update
impact: Branch 2 filters `updates` to a hand-maintained managed_field_names set and, if ANY managed key is present, routes only that subset to update_room_fields and RETURNS -- so every non-managed key in the same call is discarded with no error and no log, and the generic merge branch below is unreachable for that call. _async_update_room({'enabled': True, 'color': '#ff0000'}) persists enabled, drops color, saves, and writes state reporting success. Currently LATENT: every in-scope caller passes a single key. The risk is that this is a BASE CLASS with a permissive default, inherited by the room history and rule-status sensors too -- exactly the shape that turns a future one-line caller into a silent wrong answer. The asymmetry names it: the profile_name branch above guards with len(updates) == 1 precisely to stop swallowing companions; branch 2 does not. Branch 2 also skips the summary rebuild that the generic branch performs.

title: Hand-copied room defaults, including two that disagree about the same missing key
impact: extra_state_attributes re-declares defaults by hand rather than deriving them: profile_name defaults to the literal 'vacuum_quick' where the canonical DEFAULT_ROOM_PROFILE_NAME is imported properly by three other modules -- and this is also the BRAND-default question, since adapters declare their own default_profile, so a brand naming a different default would still have every room entity report vacuum_quick. floor_type defaults to 'hardwood' at :218 and to '' at :226, eight lines apart. Most consequential: order defaults to 0 here and in number.py:170, while entity_helpers.sort_room_items, queue_engine, run_plan and profiles/manager all default it to 999 -- so a room record missing `order` would be shown as 'cleans first' by the control the user sees and treated as 'cleans last' by the engine that dispatches. All three are LATENT: build_managed_rooms always writes the keys and the load-time backfill setdefaults two of them -- though that backfill is itself a third hand-copy of the same literals rather than an import.

wontfix: KILLED — the reachability premise is fatal to the claim AS RECORDED. Stage B's reproducer executed it: import_theme does `name = str(source_theme.get('name','')).strip()` (themes/manager.py:537), so a JSON null becomes the STRING 'None', which is truthy and passes the `if not name` gate. The stated entry path — 'reachable via a hand-edited import' — cannot produce the defect. That sentence was mine and it was wrong. Split from the original SN-10 so Corpus C does not have to assert the LINE is correct; the line-level defect survives as SN-10b.
title: KILLED: the claim that a hand-edited theme import can store a raw null name
impact: Split half A of the original SN-10. Kill reason: KILLED_INVALID_REPRODUCER — the reachability path was never executable. Retained as negative evidence and as a killed_lookalike for any future absent-is-not-None family, because it is a case where the line-level reasoning was sound and only the entry vector was fabricated.

title: A raw stored null theme name renders as the string 'None' — valid, but not reachable in normal operation
impact: Split half B of the original SN-10, and the half both lenses agreed on. `str(entry.get('name', 'none'))` returns Python's str(None) == 'None' for a stored null rather than the intended 'none', and an empty string yields an empty state. CONFIRMED_EXECUTED by Stage B's reproducer at the line. REACHABILITY IS THE NARROW PART: no writer can produce it — import_theme stringifies, and _normalize_theme_entry gates stored entries — so it requires a direct .storage edit (discouraged; see the never-edit-.storage rule) or legacy pre-normalization data. Fix is one expression: `(entry.get('name') or 'none')`, which also handles the empty-string case. Low reachability, real defect, trivial repair — a candidate for `document_only` if Chris prefers.

title: The job-active warning asserts a run-time failure that is unreachable from the state triggering it — and computes presence from a stale snapshot
impact:
SETTLED ON HARDWARE. THE SYSTEM BEHAVES CORRECTLY; THIS IS A REPORTING-LAYER DEFECT ONLY.

When a Roborock idles out it drops the cloud connection and the upstream integration REMOVES the entities — HA reports them as no-longer-provided and vacuum.<vac> becomes a restored stub. Every layer reports this honestly: the integration says the entity stopped being provided, the card says no map is loaded, and binary_sensor.<vac>_cleaning is genuinely absent. See reference_roborock_idle_disconnect.md.

(1) THE WARNING IS UNREACHABLE-BY-CONSTRUCTION. It says "EVERY run will strand (never finalize). Check the upstream integration didn't drop this entity." But from that state NO RUN CAN BE STARTED — vacuum.<vac> is a restored stub with no platform behind it, so the dispatch service call has nothing to reach. The warning describes a run-time failure mode in a state where runs cannot be initiated, and its remedial advice points at an upstream regression when the real cause is an idle device that a single wake resolves. Cost: three successive wrong diagnoses in this campaign.

(2) RESIDUAL, AND THE PART WORTH FIXING: presence is computed from the wrong source. diagnostics.py:364 reads the LIVE adapter config for the entity id; :365 reads entity_resolution, built from get_vacuum_capabilities(refresh=False) — a STORED snapshot whose entity map lacks the job_active key entirely. That is latent today but WOULD produce a genuinely false alarm any time the snapshot lags while the entity exists. Same root as DR-DIAG-1; belongs in that cluster.

LOW because no user-visible product behaviour is wrong — only the wording of one diagnostic string and a latent source-of-truth error behind it. Fix: resolve job_active from hass.states via the adapter-declared id (as :364 already does), and reword to state the observed condition — device appears disconnected, wake it — instead of asserting permanent failure.

title: The exactly-once finalize claim releases BEFORE the permanent gate is written, and an await sits in the gap - the finalize body runs twice
impact:
PROVEN ON HARDWARE AND BY SOURCE TRACE, 2026-07-31. REOPENS THE CAMPAIGN CRIT DECLARED FULLY CLOSED AT 71e089c.

HARDWARE EVIDENCE (.claude/notes/_frozen/baseline/ivy-run-BEFORE.log): the finalize body ran TWICE for each of two jobs. job_2026-07-31T20-14-28 auto-finalized at 20:16:13.339 and .342; job_2026-07-31T20-16-17 at 20:18:46.275 and .289. All four emissions carry a full completed_job payload - none carries reason=finalize_in_flight or already_finalized - so these are not rejected duplicates, the body ran. Body-side writes doubled to match ('Incomplete run log written' x2, 'Trouble rooms log updated' x2 per job). Control: Alfred's capture shows each exactly once. Second control: within the same Ivy capture only LISTENER-driven handlers doubled; SERVICE-driven ones did not (start_selected_rooms and its debug.span open/close each appear once), which rules out the flight recorder duplicating records.

MECHANISM. In listeners/lifecycle.py::_process --
  L316  await finalize_learning_for_active_job(...)  -> claim taken, body runs, and its
        finally (learning/manager.py:737-741) POPS finalize_claimed_at
  L322  _LOGGER.debug('Auto-finalized job ...')      -> synchronous
  L334  finally: await hass.async_add_executor_job(tracker.end_job, ...)
        -> EXECUTOR ROUND-TRIP. THIS YIELDS THE EVENT LOOP.
  L349  mark_active_job_finalized(...)               -> only HERE is finalized=True
        written (jobs/active_job.py:2035, in place on the same dict)

One physical event (cancel-and-dock) changes several of the up-to-six entities watched by the single lifecycle listener (listeners/_common.py get_lifecycle_watch_entities: vacuum entity, task_status, dock_status, active_cleaning_target, active_map, job_active). The handler fires once PER ENTITY, each spawning _process(). Task B resumes during Task A's yield at L339 and finds started_at present, finalized NOT yet set, and finalize_claimed_at ALREADY POPPED. All three checks pass, so B takes the claim and runs the body a second time.

THE COMMENT IS THE BUG. learning/manager.py:738 asserts 'After a successful finalize `finalized` is the gate, so releasing does not reopen it.' That is false as written: finalized is not set by the claim holder, it is set by the CALLER, in a different module, after an await. The claim is airtight inside its own function and the guarantee evaporates the moment it returns.

NOT A ROBOROCK DEFECT - DO NOT SCOPE THE REPAIR TO THE ADAPTER. The race is in brand-agnostic code. Roborock's cancel-and-dock merely flips enough watched entities close enough together to interleave two handler invocations. Eufy is not safe; it was luckier in this capture.

IMPACT. Every affected job is ingested into learning twice - room timings, battery metrics, cleaning area, and trouble-room counters all double-counted. This is corruption of the learning model, the exact failure class Waves 0-3b were built to prevent.

FIX SHAPE (packet decision, not implemented). Write finalized inside the claimed window, or release the claim only on the failure path - which keeps a transient failure retryable while leaving success permanently gated.

HYPOTHESES REFUTED ALONG THE WAY, recorded so they are not re-tried: (a) a str(map_id) key mismatch making _stored_job None - impossible, because get_active_job() does the same lookup first and its default state has no started_at, so a miss returns reason=missing_started_at without ever emitting a completed_job; (b) two distinct map buckets finalizing legitimately - both emissions per job log the same map and job_id; (c) a 71e089c-style wrapper bypass - core/manager.py:4666 does await the chokepoint.

SEPARATE, STILL OPEN: the claim block at learning/manager.py:702 is wrapped in `if _stored_job is not None:` with NO else branch, so a None lookup skips the claim entirely. A real structural hole, but not the one that fired here.

Full record: .claude/notes/_frozen/baseline/phase-b-ivy-coverage.json (OBS-IVY-1).

brands: eufy (Roborock declares no code tables, so it degrades to 'trust the run')
title: total_error_seconds is subtracted from cleaning_time_seconds with no notion of WHOSE fault it was, so a station fault raised while the robot cleaned normally is charged against the robot's cleaning time
impact: Found by LIVE OBSERVATION, not by an audit -- which is why it had no corpus row until 2026-08-04 and RP-046 could never credit (its finding_id 'live:DOCK-1' resolved to nothing, so the packet was structurally uncloseable AND the finding rendered nowhere as open: invisible in both directions). Evidence: alfred job_2026-08-01T23-23-35, archived in _frozen/baseline/. The robot cleaned the kitchen for 360 s, covered 4.0 m2, drew 3% battery and used 30.8 ml of mop water. The record says it cleaned for ZERO seconds: cleaning_time_seconds_raw 360, total_error_seconds 455, cleaning_time_seconds max(0, 360-455) = 0. Five faults, all code 6013 STATION CLEAN WATER PUMP SHORT, at job-elapsed 72/83/478/486/525 s -- the station's clean-water pump complained while the robot worked through it. used_for_learning was TRUE, so the model learned that 4 m2 takes no time. PARTLY FIXED since: the evidence axis (invalidating/safe/unclassified) now gates the subtraction and is reported as error_seconds_by_evidence. The SOURCE axis (dock/robot/unknown) is still unwired -- eufy_error_source() exists in adapters/eufy/vocabulary.py:515 with ZERO callers -- so a user cannot see that 455 s of fault came from their dock rather than their robot.

title: Companion entities are resolved by deriving a name from the vacuum entity id, with no device-registry lookup and no fallback — a device whose entities are named differently reports EVERY capability as absent, silently
impact: build_entity_id does string surgery: vacuum_entity_id.split('.')[-1] + suffix. There is no registry lookup, no fallback, and no signal when a derived name does not exist — the capability is simply reported absent. PROVEN INCOMPLETE ON THE MAINTAINER'S OWN INSTALL (2026-08-04): all 65 robovac_mqtt entities share a device_id with vacuum.alfred, and at least three are AREA-PREFIXED and therefore underivable — camera.dining_room_alfred_map, select.dining_room_alfred_switch_map, sensor.dining_room_alfred_total_cleaning_area. It goes unnoticed only because the adapter does not currently declare those particular entities. Suspected live impact, issue #48 (ptruman, X10 Pro Omni, vacuum.robovac_x10_pro_omni): ALL TEN declared companions resolved to exists=False, so the install was classified as reduced/scalar transport and reported supports_water_control False and supports_mop_features False on a machine that has both — while the user could see a water level entity in Developer Tools. Not confirmed as the cause there (a genuine reduced transport produces the same diagnostics, which is DIAG-1), but the derivation is defective independently of that. FIX SHAPE: resolve through the entity registry by device_id, keep the derived name as a fallback. Wants care — device-scoped matching must still pick the right entity when a device exposes two plausible candidates, and it changes resolution for every Eufy install.

title: entity_resolution reports only what the adapter DERIVED, so 'we looked in the wrong place' is indistinguishable from 'this device has no such entity'
impact: The dump lists each declared companion with exists true/false. It never lists what the vacuum's DEVICE actually exposes, so a naming miss and a genuinely absent capability produce byte-identical output. Issue #48 is the demonstration: ten entities at exists=False could mean a reduced-transport device (nothing to fix) or a resolution failure (ENT-1, affecting anyone whose entity naming differs) — and answering it required going back to the user for entity ids the diagnostics could have carried. FIX: alongside entity_resolution, list the entities sharing a device_id with the vacuum entity. Cheap, no behaviour change, and it makes the NEXT report of this class self-diagnosing instead of costing a round trip.

title: The tRaw docstring claims it escapes interpolated values; it does not — neither t() nor tRaw() escapes vars
impact: NOT a live vulnerability — every tRaw call site checked (bindings/setup.js's ~12 failed_* handlers, bindings/map.js, room-access, room-rules, room-editor) lands in a sink that escapes: renderers/setup.js:126 escapeHtml(String(error)), and the block-reason sinks in renderers/rooms.js:561/610. So the pairing tRaw + escape-at-sink is correct everywhere today. The defect is the DOCSTRING at renderers/shared.js:~69-76: 'skips string-escaping so the markup survives, but STILL escapes interpolated values.' translate() does the opposite and says so in its own comment (i18n/index.js:302 — 'Vars are inserted RAW — the caller escapes user data at the sink'). Verified by execution: translate('en', 'bind_setup.failed_add_vacuum', {error: ''}) returns the tag unescaped with AND without {raw:true}. THE TRAP: a future caller who trusts the docstring and therefore skips escapeHtml at a new sink opens the hole, and the docstring will read as justification in review. FIX: correct the docstring to state that vars are inserted raw in both t() and tRaw(), and that the SINK owns escaping; consider a lint/test that pins the escaping contract rather than describing it. Found while verifying A5-AG-2's escaping (a params-carrying block_reason key was the first tRaw call site to interpolate a user-authored value, a ROOM NAME).
